name: Helium-neon (HeNe)
era: First ran December 13, 1960 (infrared); red line 1962; used in a show by 1968; later displaced by red diodes
wavelengths: 632.8 nm red (first lased at 1,153 nm infrared)
known_for: The low-power red beam of hobby and small show systems

name: Argon-ion
era: Discovered February 14, 1964; the most common professional show laser until solid state arrived around 2000
wavelengths: 488.0 nm blue, 514.5 nm green; also 457.9 and 476.5 nm
typical_power: Up to 30 W (Coherent Sabre, 1990s); 6 W (Star II)
cooling: Water, several gallons per minute; three-phase power; about 0.05% efficient
known_for: Cyan beam split into blue and green with a dichroic or prism

name: Krypton-ion
era: In show use by 1969; gave way to solid state around 2000
known_for: Red and yellow for gas-era shows

name: Mixed-gas argon/krypton (white light)
wavelengths: Argon and krypton lines from one tube; optics chosen for about 55% red, 20% green, 25% blue-violet
known_for: Full color from a single tube

name: Copper vapor
typical_power: Ten to hundreds of watts, pulsed at 5-30 kHz (2001)

name: Frequency-doubled Nd:YAG
typical_power: Up to 60 W average at 20 kHz, pulsed
known_for: High-power green for large outdoor shows; five were used at Everland

name: DPSS (diode-pumped solid state)
era: Reached shows in the late 1990s; drove the move away from gas around 2000
wavelengths: 532 nm green (808 nm pump, 1064 nm fundamental); also 473 and 457 nm blue, 671 nm red
cooling: Temperature-sensitive crystals; ran from a standard outlet by 2004
known_for: Smaller, more efficient and cheaper than ion lasers

name: Direct diode
era: First InGaN diode 1995 or 1996; blue first, show-industry switch to green diodes dated to 2013
wavelengths: Red 637-638 nm, green 520-525 nm, blue 445-455 nm
typical_power: About 120 mW to 1.5 W per diode; combined into projectors of 3 W to 270 W (2023)
cooling: No crystal temperature control; less heat than DPSS
known_for: The current standard for professional show projectors; modulated directly

name: OPSL (optically pumped semiconductor laser)
era: First shipped by Coherent in 2002; over 150,000 in the field by November 2023
cooling: Gain chip mounted on a heat sink
known_for: Round, high-quality beam at about 0.2 mrad, and yellow and orange that diodes do not offer

name: Fiber
known_for: Listed by ILDA with OPSL at about 0.2 mrad divergence
